items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Our trio... was engaged along with a singer, Madame Claude Alphand... We accompanied Gwyn who sang five numbers.

ctx.x: A club in the village called Tony Pastors started giving Sunday afternoon jam sessions, which were presented by Frank Newton, and some well known names assisted at these get-togethers. Sessions were jumping also in the Village Vanguard, Eddie Condon's club and Nick's all situated in Greenwich Village.

The owner of the Village Vanguard, Max Gordon, and a naturalized Frenchman named Herbert Jacoby opened a swank club at 152 East 55th Street, the same address as the club that Rodger Kay had put a band in and the joint folded shortly after I joined the band. This club was called the Blue Angel and it clicked with the high society the first night it opened. Our trio, which was known as Ellis Larkins' trio, was engaged along with a singer, Madame Claude Alphand, whom I was told, was the wife of the French ambassador…

This was the easiest job I ever had during my many years as a jazz musician, and the 52nd street musicians were really jealous because we didn't start working until 10:30 pm and if we went to the White Rose, which we did almost every night when we finished at the club, we were there at 2 am. We played a set for one hour and the attractions went on at 11:30. Madame Alphand had her own accompanist and the Bernards didn't need/for their act. We accompanied Gwyn who sang five numbers. There was a commercial pianist…
